items.blurb: Mallika Rao explains that the true complexity of adaptive recommendation systems lies outside model architecture.

items.title: Cloudflare Details Its Migration from WordPress to EmDash
items.blurb: Cloudflare recently documented the migration of its main blog from WordPress to EmDash, the open source content management system developed internally.

items.title: Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app
items.blurb: How we rebuilt the diff surface in the GitHub Copilot app to open a million-line pull request with hundreds of inline review comments. The post Rendering huge pull requests in the GitHub Copilot app appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

items.title: Trading a Cloud Identity for Your Own: Workload Attestation on Managed Compute
GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to build custom workflows with canvases
items.blurb: Describe the interface you need in plain English, then let the agent build a live surface you can both use and update—so you spend less time adapting to tools and more time getting work done.

items.title: Agents can now set up your website’s security with Turnstile Spin
items.blurb: Misconfiguring Turnstile by skipping backend validation leaves sites exposed to bots. Turnstile Spin fixes incomplete setups by using your preferred AI coding agent to wire up server-side verification.

items.title: Improving site performance by shipping more CSS
items.blurb: How we fully migrated github.com away from CSS-in-JS. The post Improving site performance by shipping more CSS appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

items.title: Home Made CobbleDB Replaces DynamoDB at Perplexity to Cut Query Latency 5x and Reduce Cloud Storage
items.blurb: Perplexity has migrated its search infrastructure from Amazon DynamoDB to CobbleDB, an internally developed key-value store in Rust. This change reduced latency and costs associated with handling large document batches.

items.title: Stateless MCP Removes Session Affinity Requirements for AWS Server Deployments
items.blurb: AWS details how the latest Model Context Protocol specification removes protocol-level sessions, sticky-session requirements, and session storage for remote MCP servers.

items.title: Microservices are organizational debt disguised as architecture.
items.blurb: Every time I’ve seen microservices pitched, it sounds great on paper. Independent teams, clean ownership, scale only what you need.
